description:
src/async_fetcher.rs:139-145: `AsyncRevocationChecker::check_revocation_against_anchor` defaults to `Ok(())`. Same shape as the sync `pkix_revocation::RevocationChecker` — and same footgun.

Scenario: a consumer writes `impl AsyncRevocationChecker for MyChecker` providing only check_revocation. The anchor-issued certificate (the intermediate CA directly signed by the root) is silently NOT revocation-checked. A trust anchor's directly-issued certificate is the most security-sensitive cert in the chain — if that intermediate is compromised, every cert under it is mis-trusted. Defaulting that path to Ok(()) is the wrong default for a security primitive.

The rustdoc warns about this but the warning is buried in the trait docs. Anyone copy-pasting the trait impl from another consumer's code or from a tutorial will hit this and not notice. Real-world consumers of this trait will get this wrong eventually.

This is inherited from the sync trait in pkix-revocation, which already has the same problem (out of scope for THIS review). What is in scope: the async trait could deliberately diverge — make check_revocation_against_anchor non-default, force every impl to make an explicit choice. Pre-1.0 trait change. The sync trait stays as is; the async trait, being newly added in this diff, is the right place to fix the pattern without breaking existing consumers.

Recommendation: remove the default. Or, if keeping the default for ergonomic reasons, make it `unimplemented!()` — a runtime panic on first invocation is louder than silent Ok.
title: Async checker default check_revocation_against_anchor=Ok(()) replicates known footgun
